case_name: Munna Kumar @ Avinash Kumar vs Ruby Kumari & Anr
facts_of_case: Petitioner claimed maintenance under section 24 of the Hindu Marriages Act. Trial court directed father to pay maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: The rigours of Section 24 of the Hindu Marriages Act cannot be avoided merely because a person claims that the marriage was void.
legal_principles.held: Such reasoning of the court below, in fact, seems to be absolutely correct that merely because when a person i.e. husband will come out with a defence that the marriage at the inception was void, rigours of section 24 of the Hindu Marriages Act cannot be avoided.

legal_principles.principle: A father who files a suit on behalf of his minor son is not entitled to disown liability for paying maintenance.
legal_principles.held: When an order has been passed directing that the petitioner, a minor, who is pursuing his matrimonial case through his natural guardian i.e. his father, the father cannot disown the liability of paying maintenance which actually has been directed against the petitioner.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order 32 Rule 1

outcome.final_order: Impugned order does not suffer from any jurisdictional error.

keywords: pater est qui etiam post partum
